queue.arrival_vs_drain: arrival ~30/h (proposal.created) vs drain ~25/h (step.succeeded) - backlog still compounding

quality.note: sample window now mixes mock and non-mock (52% mock prefix hit rate vs 100% in prior cycle's 1000-sample) - adapter appears partially bypassed

opportunities.finding: Backlog has doubled in one cycle: 73 -> 152 queued, oldest now 454min (08:45Z), p50 wait 238min, p90 432min. All 6 running steps are stale (>30min without update, including two frozen draft_tweet steps from 2026-06-20 and 2026-10-09). 59 missions created in the last 3h have 0 terminal. Latency, not deadlock, is the constraint - but at p50 238min no experiment result is actionable inside a business day.

First non-mock artifacts appeared: 52% of sampled 3h events no longer carry the literal '[mock-llm]' prefix (prior cycle measured 100%). A real LLM path is partially live. This is the first signal that the pipeline can produce genuine content - and it is happening unannounced, with no measurement of whether real insights beat placeholders on any outcome.

The publish funnel still has zero rows end-to-end: 0 tweet.posted events ever, 0 ops_social_posts rows, while 2 tweet drafts were created this hour and the post_tweet gate (x_daily_quota limit 8/day, 0 used) is open. The single cheapest growth datapoint - one real post - is still unclaimed. Publishing one mock-vs-real A/B pair is the smallest experiment that produces a genuine funnel row.

Proposal creation is outpacing value: 32 proposals in the last hour versus 26 insights generated and 1 content draft, with 2 tweet drafts. The org is manufacturing analysis faster than it converts analysis into shipped artifacts. Cutting proposal volume 30% would not reduce learning, only queue pressure.

risks.risk: Critical: queue latency is now past the point where cycle outputs feed the next cycle. A 238min p50 wait means the intel this cycle is describing a backlog state that will have changed twice before it is acted on; compounding growth decisions on it will chase stale signals.

High: two running draft_tweet steps have been frozen since 2026-06-20 and 2026-10-09, and 6/6 running steps are stale. If those are holding claims, they explain the queue growth directly and are a trivial fix (reaper) versus a capacity problem.

High: the mock-to-real LLM transition is unmeasured. Real output and placeholder output currently coexist in the same event stream with no flag separating them, so every metric computed over the last cycle is a blend of two incomparable populations.

Medium: the publish path has been 'ready' for many cycles and still shows zero external side effects. If the mock-llm text was the de-facto reason nothing was published, fixing the adapter without shipping the first post leaves the funnel permanently unmeasured.

decision: Queue is the growth constraint, not content generation. The org already produces ~26 insights/h; what it lacks is (a) freed claim capacity from stale steps and (b) one real published artifact. E1 and E2 together are ~1h of work and would replace every downstream metric with a trustworthy one. Ship E1 first, then E2 within the same cycle.
